interest: This file provides valuable insight into interwar naval diplomacy and public relations between the United States and Japan in 1933, shortly after Japan's withdrawal from the League of Nations. It documents the goodwill cruise of the Imperial Japanese Navy's Training Squadron (the cruisers Iwate and Yakumo) through Mexican ports and the strategically sensitive Panama Canal Zone. Vice Admiral Hyakutake's luncheon address at Balboa offers a striking example of official amity rhetoric proclaiming the arrival of the 'age of the Pacific' and minimizing bilateral tensions as 'superficial' and 'temporary,' presenting a poignant contrast to the escalating strategic rivalry that culminated in the Pacific War eight years later.
overview: This file comprises State Department records from March to July 1933 concerning courtesy port visits by the Japanese Imperial Training Squadron, consisting of the cruisers Iwate and Yakumo under the command of Vice Admiral Gengo Hyakutake, to Mexican ports, American ports, and the Panama Canal Zone. The documentation includes cross-reference sheets, internal Division of Far Eastern Affairs memoranda, a diplomatic despatch from Chargé d'Affaires H. D. Finley at the American Legation in Panama, and the enclosed transcript of Vice Admiral Hyakutake's address at a luncheon hosted in Balboa by Panama Canal Governor Julian L. Schley. The records reflect the diplomatic protocol, naval courtesies, and public rhetoric emphasizing peaceful cooperation and mutual understanding in the Pacific between the United States and Japan during the interwar period.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting that Panama despatch No. 1548 regarding the visit of Japanese cruisers Iwate and Yakumo to the Canal Zone is filed under 819.00-General Conditions/95.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet directs researchers to file 819.00-General Conditions/95 for despatch No. 1548 dated June 16, 1933, from Roy T. Davis in Panama. The referenced despatch concerns the visit of the Japanese cruisers Iwate and Yakumo to the Panama Canal Zone. It specifically notes comments on speeches delivered during official receptions held during the visit.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Despatch No. 1548 Regarding Japanese Cruisers' Visit

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum summarizing Panama Legation despatch No. 1580 enclosing Vice Admiral Hyakutake's luncheon address.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (CRB / CAB)
subfiles.summary: This internal memorandum from the Division of Far Eastern Affairs summarizes despatch No. 1580 of July 15, 1933, from the Legation at Panama. It notes that the despatch transmitted the text of an address given by Vice Admiral Hyakutake, commander of the Japanese cruisers Iwate and Yakumo. The memorandum highlights Hyakutake's gratitude for the cordial welcome and his expressed hopes for enhanced American-Japanese amity in the Pacific region.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Despatch No. 1580 Enclosing Admiral Hyakutake's Address
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (DEC / MCH)

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting the text of remarks made by Vice Admiral Hyakutake at a luncheon hosted by Governor Schley in Balboa.
subfiles.from: H. D. Finley (Chargé d'Affaires a.i., Legation of the United States of America, Panama)
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 1580 from the American Legation at Panama references previous reporting in despatch No. 1548 regarding the visit of the Japanese cruisers Iwate and Yakumo to Balboa from May 13 to May 19, 1933. Chargé d'Affaires ad interim H. D. Finley reports that he has obtained the text of the remarks delivered by Vice Admiral Hyakutake during a luncheon hosted in his honor by Panama Canal Governor Schley on May 15, 1933. A copy of the address is enclosed for the Department of State.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1580 Transmitting Remarks of Japanese Admiral Hyakutake

subfiles.about: Transcript of remarks delivered by Vice Admiral Hyakutake at a luncheon tendered by Panama Canal Governor Julian L. Schley in Balboa.
subfiles.summary: In this address delivered at Governor Schley's luncheon in Balboa, Vice Admiral Hyakutake expresses deep appreciation on behalf of the Imperial Training Squadron for the hospitable welcome extended in the Canal Zone. He praises the canal administrators and prominent citizens whose wisdom and energy developed the waterway. Hyakutake proclaims that the 'age of the Pacific' is arriving, insisting that the Pacific Ocean should serve as a highway for mutual advancement rather than conflict, and asserts that past irritations between the United States and Japan were merely superficial and temporary.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 1580: Address of Vice Admiral Hyakutake at Governor Schley's Luncheon
subfiles.to: Governor Julian L. Schley and luncheon guests

subfiles.about: Far Eastern Affairs memorandum reporting Mexican and American permission for Japanese warships to make courtesy calls at their respective ports.
subfiles.summary: This State Department Division of Far Eastern Affairs memorandum records that the Mexican Government granted permission for the Japanese gunboats (cruisers) Yakumo and Iwate to make courtesy visits to Mexican ports, based on Mexico City despatch No. 2338. It also notes that the United States Government had granted permission for visits by the same vessels to American ports. Furthermore, it records that the Japanese Minister at Mexico City intended to host an official reception for the visiting Japanese Admiral and his staff.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Mexican and American Port Visits by Japanese Warships Yokumo and Iwate
subfiles.to: Department of State / Office of Naval Intelligence (ONI / MEN)
